title: PostgreSQL delivery and readback: clear, write, read back in one project
proves: a project declares one PostgreSQL client in the entry and uses it in three steps: clear the table, write the orders, read them back
a normal run writes 12 rows to the table and the readback returns 12 rows; a second run clears first and gives the same rows

the run checks values: an <assert> on every readback row and an <assert> on a totals row (row count, id sum, amount sum, status count); a failed assert stops a normal run (negative run_assert_total_wrong)

Build reads the table (seed.sql, the 12 rows that the seed writes) and proves the readback product against it; it isolates the write and skips the clear, so it does not prove that the load wrote the rows
the table comes from db/seed.sql, which the test runs before Build and the runs, because Build refuses an <execute> step (unsupported_bounded_operation)
the literal count on the readback works around #493 and is marked in the XML
this project needs the PostgreSQL service: it runs in the external-service test job

negatives.name: run_assert_total_wrong
negatives.expected: The table does not hold the rows that the load writes
negatives.run_error: The table does not hold the rows that the load writes
